title: Demonstrate, hand over, and test your independence
outcome: Defend a working capstone and identify the skills that still need practice.
story: Amina wants a teammate to run the product after your visit. A hiring reviewer also wants to see whether you can make and explain a change without following a solution.

frames.explanation: Course completion is a practice record. Independent performance supplies different evidence.
A useful review ends with a concrete next task when a skill is not demonstrated.

sections.title: Demonstrate the customer outcome
paragraphs: Start the demo with the original problem and baseline. Show the main operation with realistic safe data, then one denied case and one recoverable failure. Explain what improved and what remains limited.

Be honest about the mode: an offline extractive or fixture demonstration does not prove real-model quality. Show the separate real-provider evaluation if you ran it. Give the reviewer the commit and commands needed to reproduce your claims.

sections.title: Hand over operation and ownership
paragraphs: Provide setup, architecture, API contract, data model, configuration placeholders, evaluation command, known limits, and recovery steps. Identify owners for deployment, incidents, data access, and policy updates.

Ask a teammate to start from a clean checkout and follow the runbook without your intervention. Record where they get stuck and improve the instructions. A handoff is successful when someone else can operate and diagnose the product.

sections.title: Complete an independent challenge
paragraphs: Choose an unseen requirement with a reviewer. Examples include expiring policies, a second shop workflow, duplicate retry protection, or a stale-response bug. Agree on acceptance before coding; do not open the course solution for that challenge.

You may use AI tools, as working engineers do. Keep a short record of suggestions you checked or rejected. Explain the code, tests, boundaries, tradeoffs, and one failure investigation in your own words. Independence means owning the result, not avoiding all tools.

sections.title: Use a readiness review with evidence
paragraphs: Review build, debugging, data, security, AI evaluation, delivery/recovery, explanation/handoff, and independent change. For each skill attach a reproducible artifact and have a reviewer verify it. A checked box or function output cannot verify that evidence.

The exercise practices a completeness rule. Its ready flag means the supplied records meet that rule, not that someone is guaranteed a job. If a skill has a gap, choose targeted practice and reassess. Beyond these 30 lessons, repeat projects with unfamiliar requirements and real team review.

words.meaning: Giving another person enough knowledge and instructions to operate the product.
Verified work on a task without following its supplied solution.
A skill that has not yet been demonstrated with sufficient evidence.

example.output: ready is false; the other seven skill names appear in gaps
explanation: The review names the required skills explicitly.
Each needs a verified independent artifact record.
Missing evidence produces a practice target, not a mastery claim.

exercise.title: An evidence completeness rule
exercise.brief: Write readiness(evidence). Return ready and gaps in the stated skill order: build, debug, data, security, ai, delivery, explain, independent. Each skill needs verified=true, independent=true, and a non-blank artifact string. This checks records, not the artifacts themselves.

steps.title: Require build and debugging evidence
steps.task: For this step require verified build and debug entries. Return missing skills in that order.
steps.hint: Use some for each required skill.

steps.title: Cover the whole review
steps.task: Require all eight skills and a non-blank artifact string for each.
steps.hint: The artifact is a link or reproducible report reference; a reviewer must inspect it.

steps.title: Require independent work
steps.task: Each matching entry also needs independent === true. A completed tutorial alone does not qualify.
steps.hint: Check all requirements on the same entry.

cases.label: Two verified basics
cases.why: The intermediate rule begins with two skills.

cases.label: A complete reviewed record set
cases.why: All supplied records meet the completeness contract.

cases.label: A blank AI artifact
cases.why: A flag without an artifact is insufficient.

project.title: A reviewer-run capstone and unseen change
project.brief: Complete an independent requirement, demonstrate the product, and have another person verify the handoff and eight-skill readiness review.
deliverables: An independent change with acceptance and tests.
A reproducible demo and handoff package.
A reviewer-verified skill report and next-practice plan.

milestones.title: Own an unseen task
actions: Agree on a new requirement and acceptance.
Build and debug without its reference solution.
Record AI assistance and how you checked it.

milestones.title: Hand over the system
actions: Have a reviewer run a clean checkout.
Show main, denied, and failed/recovered paths.
Explain architecture, data, evaluation, and release decisions.

milestones.title: Review readiness
actions: Attach evidence for all eight skills.
Ask the reviewer to reproduce important claims.
Choose a targeted project for each unverified skill.

acceptance: The change meets independently agreed acceptance.
You can explain and debug its code.
A reviewer can run the project and recovery instructions.
AI quality claims match the actual execution mode.
The review identifies verified skills and unresolved gaps.

tests.situation: Reviewer starts from a clean checkout
tests.expected: The runbook works without hidden setup.
You can adapt and explain the tradeoff.

tests.situation: A skill has no independent evidence
tests.expected: It remains a gap with a concrete practice task.

project.extension: Build a second capstone for a different customer workflow, work with a teammate, and repeat the independent review before applying the readiness claim to that context.
reflection: Which skill did the reviewer verify most convincingly?
What can you explain and change without the course solution?
